question.text: An SIA who is aggrieved by a SIAB disciplinary order imposing a three-year debarment from the empanelled list has the right to:

answer.text: Seek direct Supreme Court intervention within 15 days.
No appeal; all SIAB orders are final and binding.
Appeal to the prescribed appellate authority under the SIAB disciplinary mechanism, and ultimately approach the Securities Appellate Tribunal / Courts as applicable.
Request a re-run of the hearing by the same panel that passed the debarment order.

explanation.text: The Logic: Conceptually, a person aggrieved by a professional disciplinary order is entitled, under natural-justice principles, to an appeal before an appellate authority specified in the disciplinary scheme. For SEBI-side action against securities-market intermediaries, the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) is the statutory appellate forum, with further recourse to higher courts. Direct Supreme Court access or denial of appeal would skip the statutory hierarchy. The Trap: Seeking direct Supreme Court intervention within 15 days bypasses the statutory hierarchy. Treating all SIAB orders as final and binding contradicts natural justice. A re-run by the same panel is not an independent review. Note: The Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) does not, on the pages reviewed, set out a specific "SIAB debarment appeal route" with a named appellate authority and SAT / court escalation. Page 114 only treats disciplinary cases / sanctions as an empanelment factor; pages 213 and 220 cover generic SEBI Act penalty / adjudication powers. The reasoning above reflects general appellate-architecture practice rather than a direct workbook citation.
